Subject: Data residency & export controls — follow-up + next steps

Hi Lena / Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of requirements (as I understood them):
- Acme Health needs EU-hosted inference for patient data and must avoid transfers outside the EEA without appropriate safeguards (SCCs / contractual controls).
- You requested SOC 2 Type II evidence and confirmation about HIPAA coverage / BAA for PHI processing.
- You asked about export controls (OFAC/ITAR) and whether Redwood’s runtime or model variants introduce restrictions for cross-border work.

Redwood answers / next steps:
1) Data residency: We have an EU deployment region (Frankfurt and Amsterdam options). We can pin inference to an EU-only pool for the PoC and production to prevent egress to non-EU locations.
2) SOC 2 / HIPAA: Attaching our latest SOC 2 report (redacted). We also support HIPAA workloads and can sign a BAA — legal will follow up for contracting.
3) Vendor security questionnaire: If you can share the questionnaire we’ll have it completed by our security team; attaching the typical questionnaire template we fill in to speed things up.
4) Export controls: At a high level, Redwood does not impose additional OFAC/ITAR restrictions on model hosting beyond standard export controls for software/data. We’ll confirm specifics with legal for any edge-case territories.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll assign Markus (SE) to scope the EU PoC (env, sample SLOs, keys).
- Vivek (legal) will loop in to scope the BAA and SCCs for cross-border transfers.
- If you can send the vendor security questionnaire and any compliance checklist, we’ll prioritize completion (target: 3 business days).

Attachments: SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (redacted), Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Template.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- EU-only hosting is a hard requirement for patient data in production. For the PoC we can consider pseudonymized datasets, but for any real PHI it must remain in the EEA and under our control.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence (thank you for the redacted copy). Additionally, we require proof of annual penetration testing and an inventory of subprocessors.
- HIPAA / BAA: as a US/EU hybrid org we require a signed BAA for any PHI processing. Please have legal reach out.
- Cross-border transfers: we cannot have unrestricted transfers to the US unless SCCs are in place and our DPO signs off.
- Export controls: Acme is not ITAR-controlled, but we do operate in regions where OFAC sanctions screening is relevant — please confirm you screen accounts and flagged data flows.

I’m attaching the vendor security questionnaire (filled in with a few initial flags we’d like clarified). Please have your security/compliance SME review items around subprocessors, encryption key ownership (KMS/HSM options), and data deletion/retention policies.

Attached: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Initial.xlsx

Thanks — can Markus coordinate the PoC scope and timeline? Ideally we’d start a technical PoC in the EU region within two weeks.

Regards,
Lena Müller
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Health
lena.mueller@acmehealth.de

Subject: Re: Data residency & export controls — follow-up + next steps

Hi Lena — thanks for the details and the questionnaire. I pulled in our security/infra notes below to address the immediate technical questions so you have everything for the PoC planning:

1) EU-only hosting: We can provision a dedicated inference pool in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and restrict network egress to EEA subnets. For the PoC we’ll provide an isolated project and a minimal sample dataset ingestion pipeline.

2) KMS / key ownership: We support two modes:
   - Customer-managed keys (via AWS KMS customer key) where key material never leaves your control (recommended for PHI).
   - Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls and HSM-backed storage for customers that prefer Redwood key management.

3) Subprocessors: Our typical subprocessor list includes cloud provider infra (region-specific), observability provider (logs retention opt-in), and model artifact CDN. We’ll provide a current inventory and subprocessors addendum for legal review.

4) Data deletion & retention: Short answer: we support configurable retention policies per dataset/route. For PHI we can set immediate deletion on request and provide retention audit logs for the timeframe you specify.

5) Export control screening: Redwood performs OFAC screening on customer account creation and flags restricted entities. We don’t currently see ITAR implications for standard LLM inference; if you have specific export-control docs we can review.

PoC proposal & timeline:
- Day 0–2: Agree on PoC dataset (pseudonymized) and success criteria (latency SLO / throughput / functional validation).
- Day 3–7: Provision EU-only environment and sample data pipeline + KMS config.
- Day 8–14: Run test scenarios, collect logs and security evidence (retention settings, access logs).

I’m available this week to kick off — proposed 30-min check-in Wednesday or Thursday.

Attachments included in thread: SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (from Marissa), Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Initial.xlsx (from Acme).

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
